niche.diet: Drifting carcass particles, zooplankton, small benthic invertebrates
niche.active: Tidal (feeds on flood, rests on ebb/slack)

body: Low-slung radial disc with six frilled arms, ciliated sensory margins, thick protective mucus coat

chains.trait: Radial frill array with six sensory arms
links: Prey arrives from any horizontal axis
Forward-facing mouth wastes captures in cross-currents
Cave walls channel 3.2 m tidal bores

skill.effect: Detects and pulls prey from any direction within 2.5 m (+15% hit chance in dark/turbid water).

chains.weakness: Vulnerable to frontal strikes when reorienting arms.
observe: Six frilled arms pulsing in slack water
Disc locks onto cave floor during ebb tide

journal.en: It does not face the current. The current feeds it from all sides.

plausibility.summary: In a confined, flow-channelled tidal conduit (F13 shelf tides; F9 flooded lava tube), prey and detritus arrive from multiple headings; radial capture surfaces with flow-sensitive margins match F20’s turbid, low-visibility benthos where pressure, touch and margin chemoreception beat vision. Sixfold symmetry is uncommon in crown-group echinoderms (mostly pentamerous) but is not physically forbidden and fits a young island radiation (F27) as convergent suspension/deposit feeding, not strict echinoderm homology.

analogues.organism: Feather stars/crinoids (Crinoidea) orient arms to oscillating currents; sea anemones (Actiniaria) use radial tentacle arrays in surge channels.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Mucus net-capture mechanism along frilled margins
links: Mucus nets require continuous ciliary beating
Ciliary beat needs constant ATP from aerobic respiration
Oxygen partial pressure reaches 0.34 bar via tidal flushing

skill.effect: Shoots adhesive frill tip to snag drifting carcass bits (+20% food intake, slows target).

chains.weakness: Net tangles if struck by sharp bone or rock.
observe: Iridescent strands stretch between frill edges
Carcass fragments spiral into the center

journal.en: Silk without a spinneret. The sea weaves its bread.

chains.trait: Slow benthic crawling with radial reorientation
links: High locomotor drag makes sprinting metabolically ruinous
Slow movement conserves energy in low-visibility tuff
1.6 bar atmosphere multiplies drag to water interface

skill.effect: Rides flood currents to reposition silently (+10 m movement, zero stamina cost).

chains.weakness: Cannot flee from fast predators during strong flow.
observe: Low disc presses flat against tuff floor
Frills ratchet forward like a starfish
Tracks left in silt match tidal direction

journal.en: Muscles too heavy for sprint. It lets the sea push it.

chains.trait: Tidal rhythmicity with slack-tide disc collapse
links: Slack tide removes flow cues and depletes dissolved O2
Metabolic rate must drop to survive hypoxia

skill.effect: Collapses frills into a sealed disc during slack tide (+30% stealth, reduces detection but stops feeding).

chains.weakness: Highly vulnerable to bone spines or rock attacks when collapsed.

journal.en: It sleeps when the sea holds its breath. Wake it at your peril.

plausibility.summary: Treat Corona as tidal-zone (periodically emersed on spring lows per F13), not permanently subtidal; collapse primarily on ebb/emersion and slack hypoxia; Espinodo (or spine-using predators) threaten mainly when the disc is exposed/glassy on tuff, aligning with the spring-low haunting beat.
